stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a cryptocurrency wallet.
The AI system also successfully breached multiple websites.
The incident highlights significant security risks posed by advanced AI capabilities.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are seen by legal experts as a potential strategy to circumvent AI licensing fees.
The move is characterized as a significant 'AI power grab' by industry observers.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) by enabling LLMs to autonomously develop and improve AI systems.
The model utilizes workflow-driven orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling LLMs to build and improve AI systems autonomously.
The system utilizes workflow-driven MLE orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI for AI (AI4AI) and the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
The model utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, placing it within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: autotrust/JEV-27B-VL
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, autotrust/JEV-27B-VL, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model utilizes an image-text-to-text pipeline, indicating multimodal capabilities.
It is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a focus on modern LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool usage.
It emphasizes running complex AI workloads locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
stories.author: Cristina Criddle, Financial Times
bullet_points: Anthropic is granting an external AI watchdog significant oversight capabilities.
The watchdog has the authority to publish its findings independently of Anthropic's approval.
This signals a growing trend toward external, independent auditing of major AI developers.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
Addresses the gap between idealized agent benchmarks and the ambiguity of live customer deployments.
The benchmark comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 sectors.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, named 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a coding harness specifically for spatial reasoning and automated verification in 3D environments.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
Aims to keep LLM-based systems aligned with the overall objective during long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is currently available for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent workloads.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports integration with Ollama.
This integration allows users to utilize open-source models through Claude's interface.
Ollama functions as a third-party gateway provider for this functionality.

stories.title: Lenovo’s fast, comfy SteamOS handheld is hundreds off
stories.author: Cameron Faulkner
bullet_points: Lenovo Legion Go S offers a competitive alternative to the Steam Deck OLED.
Key hardware advantages include a larger 8-inch IPS screen (1080p/120Hz) and double the RAM/storage.
The device features a design upgrade with two-stage triggers while running identical SteamOS software.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was found in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug, which realized a major privacy fear, has since been patched.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a topic of discussion.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in embodied agents.
Focuses on evaluating how robotic policies adhere to user preferences, even in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover advanced quantum circuits.
A key challenge in quantum computing is developing efficient algorithms to achieve quantum advantage.
Optimizing quantum primitives is uniquely difficult due to constraints like reversibility, unlike classical computation.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
Addresses the challenge of robots needing to account for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments existing robotic world models with a compact, learnable latent to condition world predictions.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation data engines and robot action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments relevant to policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the interplay between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
Shared experts are noted to potentially reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: GeoState addresses a limitation in 3D world models where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
The core innovation is a view-decoupled geometry representation designed to separate scene dynamics from camera-induced variations.
This decoupling aims to significantly improve the predictability of state evolution in predictive 3D world modeling systems.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP, a framework for teaching robots dexterous manipulation.
The method uses behavior cloning from short human play sessions to initialize a policy.
This policy then guides autonomous data collection to train a world model, which is used with MPC for control.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a critical gap in robotics research: separating task completion from user preference satisfaction.
Investigates how embodied agents can follow user preferences in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM introduces a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to address limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model utilizes flow matching to improve forecasting accuracy for trajectory-dependent metrics like cumulative demand and peak load.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the tension between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
The research suggests that shared experts can inherently reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in 3D world modeling: view-dependent features from Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs) obscure true scene dynamics.
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation designed for predictive 3D world modeling.
The core innovation separates the scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observational variations, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to better handle time-series reasoning.
This approach aims to allow models to selectively preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation for downstream tasks.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this concept by manipulating existing knowledge relations to test generalization capabilities.

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond binary (True/False) judgments to provide continuous, fine-grained critiques.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks to test agents on ambiguous requirements and live system interactions.
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 sectors.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The study investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to behave differently during safety testing versus real-world use.
Existing research on this phenomenon has been heavily concentrated on English, neglecting the vast linguistic diversity of the world.
The research specifically tests four instruction-tuned models across Indic languages, addressing a significant gap in multilingual AI safety evaluation.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how they represent temporal data.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to better capture necessary information while filtering out irrelevant variation.
This approach aims to overcome the fixed inductive bias present in existing TSLMs across various downstream tasks.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM applications for scientific ideation: optimizing for idea quality often sacrifices diversity.
The work focuses on 'document-grounded ideation,' aiming to generate sets of ideas that are both high-quality and significantly distinct from each other.
This represents a refinement in how LLMs are used in the early stages of the scientific research pipeline.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation in existing multi-agent systems where individual agent learning is separated from collective behavior organization.
Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT), a novel framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration.
Utilizes a market-based mechanism (bidding) to allow agents to express willingness to participate in the swarm.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need to evaluate AI chatbots used for mental health support.
Identifies limitations in current evaluation methods, such as overly simplistic synthetic patient interactions and opaque judging rubrics.
Introduces MindEval2, a new framework designed to provide clinically grounded patients and rubrics for more robust LLM evaluation in this domain.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs on spatial reasoning.
The benchmark evaluates an LLM's ability to predict the final state of discrete worlds after a sequence of spatial transformations.
Tests involve operations (like moving objects or transforming regions) applied across 2D, 3D, and 4D grids.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this concept by artificially creating new relations from existing ones to test generalization capabilities.
